children: India’s tech companies raised a combined $10.3B in the first nine months of 2026 marking a 7 per cent increase over the $9.7B raised in the same period a year earlier, and 3 per cent above the $10B raised in 9M 2024, according to data by intelligence platform Tracxn.
This comes at a time when the number of funding rounds, first-time funded companies, and new Soonicorn additions all declined sharply.

Enterprise Applications, FinTech, and Enterprise Infrastructure emerged as the top-performing sectors, together anchored by 18 rounds of $100M or more, most notably Nxtra’s $1B private-equity round for data-centre expansion.

India Tech recorded 1,134 funding rounds in 9M 2026, down 38 per cent from 1,838 a year earlier, even as total dollars raised rose 7 per cent to $10.3B.  A major share of these mega-rounds came from AI Infrastructure, Digital Lending, and Payments - the clearest sign that capital is consolidating into fewer, larger, higher-conviction bets.
Seed funding fell 37 per cent to $698M, while early-stage funding rose 27 per cent to $4.2B and late-stage held roughly steady at $5.4B.

First-time funded companies dropped 30 per cent to 338 and Series A+ rounds fell 23 per cent to 409, pointing to a market that is backing proven companies over new entrants even as headline dollars edge higher.

Enterprise Infrastructure was the fastest-growing sector of the period, with funding up 436 per cent to $1.6B from $292M in the same period a year earlier, followed by Enterprise Applications, which grew 49 per cent to $3.5B, and FinTech, up 13 per cent to $2.2B.

AI Infrastructure was the single most-funded business feed at $1.2B, ahead of Digital Lending ($799M) and Payments ($773M) - a mix that places the compute-and-capital layer at the centre of India’s 9M 2026 funding story.
India minted 6 new unicorns in 9M 2026, up 50 per cent from 4 in the same period a year earlier, and did so on markedly less capital.

New unicorns raised an average of $101M before their unicorn round, less than half the $205M averaged in 9M 2025, and crossed the billion-dollar mark 4.9 years after their Series A, down from 6.6 years - a sign that India’s most valuable companies are now being built faster and more capital-efficiently.

India Tech saw 29 IPOs in 9M 2026, unchanged from each of the prior two years, alongside 91 acquisitions, down 31% from 131. The listings that closed carried weight - Fractal Analytics led with a $1.7B IPO market cap, followed by Molbio Diagnostics ($973M) and Amagi ($858M), with Shiprocket also going public in the period.

Both exit routes are opening up far earlier in a company’s life. The average time from first funding to IPO fell to 8.5 years from 13.7 a year earlier, and the average time to acquisition dropped to 6.9 years from 14.7.
On the M&A side, Innovist’s $434M sale to L’Oréal was the period’s largest acquisition, ahead of Adani Energy Solutions’ $319M purchase of IntelliSmart and UpGrad’s $218M acquisition of Unacademy.

Bengaluru remained India’s dominant funding hub in 9M 2026, capturing 43 per cent of all tech capital with $4.4B, up from 38 per cent a year earlier. Mumbai followed at $1.8B (18 per cent share), ahead of Gurugram at $1.6B - whose share doubled from 8 per cent to 16 per cent, driven almost entirely by Nxtra’s $1B round.
In Bengaluru, CRED ($540M), Rapido ($240M), and Sarvam ($234M) were the top-funded companies of the period, reinforcing the city’s lead across fintech, mobility, and AI.

title: India tech funding rises 7% to $10.3 billion in 9M 2026
